reviews.review:
Alright. This really is a hard one to rate, it's one of those middle of the road games. I'm going to push this to a "No" honestly. While there's plenty to like, too much of this experience is tainted by this forced open-world trend BioWare was on. For every good thing, there's 2 tediously boring things. You can still have a nice time with it and some mods can help make the experience less dull. On sale or part of EA Play it's definitely worth a shot. 

The combat can be fun, the new skill system is super flexible, you've got a great variety of weapons and armour. The general feel of exploring strange planets is rather good as well. Visually the game is amazing, some animations are a little stiff, mainly facial, probably from the devs pulling the original abominations back a touch.

All in all any issues the game had on launch are largely fixed. I didn't run into many bugs and those I did were minor. The wacky animations are pretty much tamed (see above). These two issues in particular sort of got the game "memed to death" right off the bat and it's hard to recover from the first impressions.

HOWEVER, with these issues cleared up the games actual issues start to shine through. It's a lot of the issues Dragon Age Inquisition had except made way worse somehow. The excessive amount of fetch quests are exhausting to the point that I'd recommend ignoring side quests that aren't companion quests. Even the companion quests suffer but you get more out of them. 

There's another review on here about this game making everything into 3s and they're 100% correct, it's honestly ridiculous how often a basic tasks becomes "use 3 terminals" or something similar. This is almost like they had a handful of quests that worked on a linear scale but they threw in these extra "Do this 3 times" to make use of the map. Similar to Inquisition the game feels so dragged out across the open world map. The maps look great but there's not a lot going on here. 

On a similar note: The amount of times you have to fly to a whole another planet only to talk to someone who then tells you to go to another planet. Towards the end in particular this gets super draining. Just let me vidcom everyone. Nearing the end each crew mate has a little heart-to-heart scene, they're nice scenes that show optimism for the initiative. These little missions would be great IF THEY WEREN'T ALL SCATTERED ACROSS EVERY PLANET IN THE GAME. You spend 2 minutes pissing around in the Galaxy Map and another 2 minutes going to the specific location for a 30 second scene. It's such a stupidly draining way to go about it. The Movie Night is another, 5 fetch quests to set it up, all on different planets. It's terrible.

Tonally the game is a bit off. Everything does comes off as pretty lighthearted. There's not a lot of serious energy going on and it can undercut the whole story and struggle. Some of the dialogue is poorly written frankly. The whole Asari Ark mission with Cora is a good example to me. In general the story just isn't all that interesting. A fair chunk of story beats it uses are very familiar if you've played the OT. The main *thing* about the Kett is something we've seen before for example. A lot of the story feels very same-y. The ‘first contact’ stuff too was so short lived it’s sad. 15 seconds after meeting the Angara on Aya and you’re already speaking the same language and are sort of chill with each other. There’s some overheard dialogue but they really under-utilised the idea that we’re the aliens now. The Rhokar (no idea how that spelt) may as well just be Batarians with how little justification their cause is given. Archon is a weak villain.It's a very clear 'Good vs Evil'. Perhaps a lot of this could be built on but with how it went we’re not getting Andromeda 2. Perhaps ME4 will give us something. 

The characters are a mixed bag. Main crew cool, outside of that? Meh. Feel this is sort of crucial for BioWare so a breakdown:
Most of the people on the Nexus? Meh, they're fine. No real stand out characters like Anderson or Aria.
The ship staff: Kallo and Gil bicker and it's a fine background distraction. Gil has more personality and it fairly likeable. Kallo is a bit flat. Lexi is alright. They literally put Natalie Dormer in the game and then have her reject you, cold that. Suvi's alright.
The main squad:
PeeBee: Fun energy but sorta underlines the whole "never takes itself seriously" issue. Still, I like her and her arc. Her romance is cute.
Liam: Weird one this. Liam is great to Ryder, acts more like a second than Cora ever does. Take Liam out though? He suddenly acts super hostile and judgemental of all your other squad members in the Nomad. I like his determination but for the sake of my opinion of him not being tainted, I just don't take him anywhere and that sucks. Top Loyalty Mission tho.
Drack: Fun old man. Not a massive amount going on but he's interesting enough.
Cora: Honestly? Don't like her, her obsession with the Asari is grating and her behaviour regarding the Pathfinder position had potential for rivalry but it just doesn't go anywhere.
Jaal: The Angara in general are OK. Jaal is sort of an extension of this. He's fine, they're all fine. Not as interesting as the Milky Way species.
Vetra: I like everything about Vetra but felt like all of it could have also been more.

I don't like the idea of comparing this cast to the OT cast. 2/3 games v 1 game. Honestly I like some of this cast more than some of the ME2 cast despite that. I have a seemingly unpopular opinion that ME2 had too many squad mates to give them all equally sufficient substance and I prefer the 6-man squads of ME1,3 and A. I'd take PeeBee, Vetra and Liam over Samara, Jacob and Miranda. Drack is sort of on par with Grunt honestly. Someone probably hates me for saying that.

But yeah, there's a lot to like here but a lot to dislike. Best way to play this game is too ironically play as little of it as you can. Bin the side quests, install some QoL mods and you'll have a fine time. It obviously doesn't stack up to the OT but I genuinely would like to see the cast of characters again. It accomplished that much. 

Upon finishing the game I genuinely want to push it to a "Yes", the final mission is actually pretty fun but I can't put aside the the massive amounts of tedium for the actual good the game gives. For every bit of good, there's a bit of bad and a bit of tedious. It's a shame really. While I'm still very sceptical on exactly now the next Mass Effect is going to connect the Milky Way with Andromeda and make room for both, I am somewhat thankful now that Andromeda isn't completely abandoned.

If you're into in depth story; lots of narrative, characters and talking. AND you want a bit of fighting and some classic RPG stats and upgrades. THEN this will suit you well if you have time to burn and you're into aliens.

This game is unplayable. Corrupt save files cause infinite load screens. I have to go back five or more saves to find a save that isn't corrupt. I would request a refund, but I got this in a bundle with Dragon Age: Inquisition, and that is no longer on sale. I spent less than eight dollars on this game and I still heavily regret this purchase.
This felt like a mass effect game.  Very glad I finally got around to play it.

UPDATE: I have now finished the main campaign and several of the side missions.  I've put in over 27 hours and still have a lot more to do in the game.  I also bought the Legendary Edition and am looking forward to playing that as well.  Andromeda is great.  I bought the Legendary Edition because if this game.  With how good this game is, the Legendary Edition will even surprise me more.  On it's own, I absolutely love this game.   If you're on the fence, then wait until it goes on sale.  But in my opinion, this game is right up there with other games I've finished like Skyrim, Death Stranding, Horizon Zero Dawn, God of War, Tomb Raider, Uncharted, Red Dead Redemption 2, Cyberpunk, Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order, and many others.  Not only do I highly recommend it, but am baffled by the negative reviews by some people.  Again, compared to many AAA games, in my opinion, this game on it's own is one of the best!

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I have played this game for 8 hours now.  I am a first-time Mass Effect gamer and really like the game.  If this game is the worst of the bunch, then I can't wait to finish this and then buy the Legendary Edition and play the first three games!  This series is great.  Wonderful graphics, great voice acting, and a terrific soundtrack.  The story is great too!  For those who like a story-based game, I highly recommend it.
